entities.evidence: The Noah who carries out the ark instructions is Lamech’s son. The source tag identifies this flood survivor.
The name יַהְוֶה identifies the God who commanded Noah. The source tag LORD@Gen.1.1 supports the same divine identity as the previous Yahweh proposal.

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the subject. The phrase כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ יַהְוֶה means “according to all that YHWH had commanded him” and identifies the instructions Noah carried out.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּעַשׂ נֹחַ, “Noah did,” נֹחַ names the subject of the masculine singular verb. The suffix ־הוּ in צִוָּהוּ, “commanded him,” refers back to Noah as the one whom Yahweh commanded.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The אֲשֶׁר clause completes כֹל by specifying what it includes. כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ יַהְוֶה means “according to everything that Yahweh had commanded him.”
analysis.morphology: Preposition כְּ prefixed to the masculine singular construct noun כֹל.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause that specifies כֹּל: Noah did according to all that YHWH had commanded him. The suffix on צִוָּהוּ refers to Noah, and כֹּל supplies the content of the command.
יַהְוֶה is the subject of צִוָּהוּ, and ־הוּ refers to Noah. Noah did everything that YHWH had commanded him.
analysis.morphology: Piel perfect, third masculine singular, with a third masculine singular object suffix ־הוּ.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ יַהְוֶה, “as Yahweh had commanded him,” יַהְוֶה names the subject of צִוָּהוּ. The suffix ־הוּ refers to Noah, who carried out the command.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel
